cues.en: So good morning, everyone. I'm James Powell. As the session chair mentioned, I've been doing PyData for a very long time. I think this is my 27th, 28th PyData conference I've attended. I believe this is the 50-something PyData talk I've given in the last four years. I don't know that that makes me a Python expert. I can tell you that we have a lot of material to cover, so I won't go very deep into my own introduction. Other than to tell you that
cues.zh: 大家早上好。我是 James Powell。正如主持人所说，我参与 PyData 已经很久了。这大概是我参加的第 27 或 28 届 PyData 大会了。我想这也是我在过去四年里做的第 50 多场 PyData 演讲。我不知道这算不算 Python 专家。不过今天我们要讲的内容很多，所以我就不多做自我介绍了。只是想告诉大家

cues.en: Even though I attend many Pi Data events and I help out in organizing all of these, I do this in the capacity of a volunteer. There are a lot of volunteer opportunities available with NumFocus and with Pi Data itself. So if you're interested in running up Pi Data in your own city or getting more involved with open source data science, please let me know or let any of the organizers of this conference know. There's always room for more volunteers.
cues.zh: 虽然我参加了许多 PyData 活动并协助组织它们，但我完全是以志愿者的身份参与的。NumFOCUS 和 PyData 本身都有大量的志愿者机会。所以如果你有兴趣在自己的城市举办 PyData，或者想更多地参与开源数据科学，请告诉我或联系本届大会的任何一位组织者。我们永远欢迎更多志愿者的加入。

cues.en: For those of you who've had the fortune or misfortune of seeing any of the talks that I've given previously at PyData events, I often give talks about strange things that you can do with Python, like embed Python interpreters within themselves, or add features to Python at runtime, or patch your Python so that you can load other Python interpreters using dynamic linker tricks. And sometimes the subtext of all of these is, you know, these are the lifestyles of the Python experts, what kind of crazy fun that we can have.
cues.zh: 对于那些有幸或不幸看过我以前在 PyData 活动上演讲的人来说，我经常会讲一些用 Python 能做的奇葩操作，比如在 Python 解释器里内嵌一个它自己，或者在运行时给 Python 添加特性，又或是给你的 Python 打补丁，好利用动态链接器的奇技淫巧来加载其他 Python 解释器。有时候这些内容的言下之意就是：看吧，这就是 Python 专家的日常，我们能玩出多疯狂的花样。

cues.en: And so I decided maybe I should give a talk that might actually be useful to an audience as opposed to just showing off some crazy things that you can do. And so one thing that might actually be useful is to really talk about what it means to be a Python expert.
cues.zh: 所以我想，也许我该做一场对观众真正有用的演讲，而不是单纯炫耀你能做哪些疯狂的事。那么真正有用的，可能就是好好聊聊究竟什么才叫 Python 专家。

cues.en: I do a good amount of, do a couple of different things in my day job. I work on a variety of different projects. I can tell you if you are an employee at Microsoft and you're interested in Python, something that I can talk to you about. Microsoft is very invested in the future of Python in more ways than you might even know. I also do some corporate training, and in that corporate training, this question of what's needed to become good at Python comes up very often. So I'm asked to answer this question for you.
cues.zh: 在日常工作中，我负责不少杂七杂八的事情，参与了各种不同的项目。如果你是 Microsoft 的员工并且对 Python 感兴趣，那我们绝对有得聊。Microsoft 对 Python 的未来投入巨大，可能远超你的想象。我平时也做一些企业培训，在培训中，“怎样才能精通 Python”这个问题经常被问到。所以今天，我就来为大家解答这个问题。

cues.en: I can tell you that what it takes to be effective in Python is pretty straightforward. To be effective in Python, that requires a certain understanding of a couple of core mental models of the language, an understanding of some of the things the language comes with, like the built-in data types and the built-in functions, a little bit of an understanding of what's available in the standard library. This talk, however, is focused on the next step. What does it take to be a little bit better than just effective? What does it take to be good at Python or an expert at Python?
cues.zh: 我可以明确告诉大家，掌握 Python 并高效使用其实非常直接。要做到高效，只需要对这门语言的几个核心心智模型有一定理解，了解它自带的一些特性，比如内置数据类型和内置函数，再稍微了解一下标准库里都有什么就行了。然而，本次演讲关注的是下一步：如何才能超越“高效”，更上一层楼？怎样才能精通 Python，成为一名 Python 专家？

cues.en: Now, I could spend the next two hours telling you in very philosophical terms what that means. And I could tell you why Python experts do things in one way or the other. We could even go very deeply into some of the meaning behind the zen of Python. But instead, what I'd like to show you more specifically is a couple of what I call, perhaps, metaphors in programming in Python. It turns out that, as many of you know, Python
cues.zh: 我现在可以用接下来的两个小时，从非常哲学的角度来向大家解释这意味着什么。我可以告诉大家为什么 Python 专家会采用某种特定的方式来做事。我们甚至可以深入探讨“Python之禅”背后的某些涵义。但我更想具体展示给大家的，是几个在 Python 编程中我称之为“隐喻”的东西。正如大家所知，Python 事实上的发展历程是……

cues.en: Though it originated as something of kind of a scripting language, just a convenience language to patch together or to orchestrate code that was written in C to write simple scripts, has since grown into a full-fledged general purpose programming language. And along the way, it's developed its own ways of thinking about certain core constructs in programming. What I'd like to do in the course of this session is show you four features of Python and the ways that an expert would think about these features.
cues.zh: 它最初诞生时有点像是一种脚本语言，只是一种把 C 语言写的代码拼凑起来或协调起来的便利用途语言，用来写写简单的脚本，但自那以后，它已经成长为一门成熟的通用编程语言了。在这一发展历程中，它针对编程中的某些核心结构，形成了自己独特的思考方式。在接下来的这场分享中，我想向大家展示 Python 的四个特性，以及专家是如何理解这些特性的。

cues.en: What I want to show you is not the syntax of these features. The purpose of this presentation is not a feature parade. It irritates me un-endlessly whenever I see somebody who's writing a book about advanced Python and the entirety of the book is chapter one. Here's a feature. Chapter two. Here's another feature. Chapter three. Here's a third feature. And the entirety of the discussion of these features is merely its formal characteristics. Oh, a generator has a yield instead of a return. Oh, you can't send a non-none value into a just-started generator. A lot of
cues.zh: 我想向大家展示的并不是这些特性的语法。这场演讲的目的不是罗列特性。每当我看到有人写进阶 Python 的书，整本书全都是第一章介绍一个特性，第二章介绍另一个特性，第三章又介绍第三个特性，我就感到无比烦躁。而他们对这些特性的所有讨论，仅仅停留在形式特征上。比如：哦，生成器用的是 yield 而不是 return；哦，你不能给刚启动的生成器传入非 None 值。充斥着大量

cues.en: fundamental details of how these features work, but very little talk about how we can conceptualize these features in the broader sense of what they mean for modeling core problems. And so what I'd like to do is I'd like to talk about four of these features that you may have seen before and a couple of the core mental models for how you can think about them and how you can think about Python as a whole and wrap all of these together.
cues.zh: 关于这些特性如何运作的基础细节，却极少探讨我们该如何从更宏观的角度去理解它们，以及它们在对核心问题建模时意味着什么。因此，我想做的是聊聊你们可能见过的其中四个特性，以及思考它们、思考整个 Python 的几个核心心智模型，并把这一切融会贯通起来。

cues.en: One thing that you'll notice is, in addition to you can probably hear I'm a little bit stuffy and a little bit sick, that's only going to exaggerate my inability to remember the syntax or the documentation for basically anything. So you may see me stumble, but part of this presentation is to see me stumble and to understand that in cases where you don't understand or you don't have the documentation memorized or some of the corner cases memorized, what really is more important for all of these features
cues.zh: 大家可能会注意到，除了能听出我鼻音有点重、感冒了之外，这只会让我更加记不住任何语法或文档。所以你们可能会看到我卡壳，但这正是本次演讲的一部分——看到我卡壳，并且明白即使你不理解、没记住文档或遗漏了一些极端情况，对于所有这些特性来说真正重要的，

cues.en: is an understanding of what they are and what they mean, and not so much all of the implementation details. Those implementation details are of course critically important when you're using a feature, but that's information that you can look up and refresh when you're actually in the middle of using that feature itself. Before I get started, I'd like to take a small survey, a small informal survey of the audience. So how many of you here are Microsoft employees?
cues.zh: 是对它们是什么、意味着什么的理解，而不是那些琐碎的实现细节。当然，在实际使用某个特性时，实现细节极其重要，但那些信息完全可以在你真正用到该特性时再去查阅和复习。在开始之前，我想在现场做个简短的、非正式的小调查。请问在座的有多少是 Microsoft 的员工？

cues.en: Almost everyone. How many of you are Microsoft employees that use Python as part of your Microsoft work? How many of you are just Microsoft employees that have seen Python used in various areas of the company but don't really have direct interaction with it yet? How many of you consider yourselves to be pretty okay at Python? How many of you consider yourself to be really good at Python? A couple people? How many people are already in the back of the room thinking, I should be in the front of the room giving a talk myself?
cues.zh: 几乎所有人都是。你们当中有多少是微软员工，而且工作里会用到 Python？有多少只是在公司各处见过别人用 Python，但自己还没真正接触过的微软员工？你们当中有多少人觉得自己 Python 水平还可以？又有多少人觉得自己 Python 学得特别好？有几个人？有多少人已经在后排心想：“我才应该站在台上做演讲吧”？

cues.en: Maybe one person, maybe one person in the front. Okay, maybe we'll have to show you something new. When it comes to those of you who've seen Python, how many of you feel like you're pretty effective in Python? I can give you a simple problem. How many of you are complete newbies, and you're like, I have no idea how to even get started with Python? Okay, for those of you who are complete newbies, you may struggle a little bit. Part of this talk does presume a...
cues.zh: 可能有一个人，前排可能有一个。好吧，那我今天可能得讲点新东西了。对于接触过 Python 的人来说，有多少人觉得自己用得挺顺手的？我给你们一个简单的问题，你们能写几个函数，甚至写一两个类，毫不费力地把问题解决掉。大部分人都是这样吗？有多少人是完全的新手，觉得“我根本不知道怎么入门 Python”？好的，对于完全新手来说，可能会听得有点吃力，因为这次演讲的一部分确实预设了……

cues.en: baseline of understanding of Python. However, I don't think that the core lessons that you'll pick up here are lessons which will be totally lost on you. There are a couple of core lessons which even those of you who are somewhat effective in Python already may yet have internalized and we might have a little bit of time to repeat those. What I want to start with is I'll start with something really, really, really basic.
cues.zh: 对 Python 有基本的理解。不过，我认为大家在这里能学到的核心内容，绝不会让你们听得一头雾水。即使是对 Python 已经运用得当的人，有些核心要点可能也还没完全内化，我们或许会花点时间再过一遍。我想先从一些非常非常基础的内容开始。

cues.en: And I'm going to start a little bit more basic than what I had planned to, just because I thought the audience might be a little bit more advanced than that. So what I'll talk about at the very beginning is something that we might call the data model. Now, what you'll see is I have all of the materials for this prepared and memorized in my brain. And unfortunately, my brain is getting older and older as time goes on. And so I've already forgotten exactly what I want to talk about. And so you'll see a little bit of roughness here.
cues.zh: 我会讲得比原计划更基础一些，原本我还以为台下的听众水平会更高一些。所以一开始我要讲的，可以称之为数据模型。大家会发现，我把这次的所有材料都准备并记在脑子里了。遗憾的是，岁月不饶人，我的脑子越来越不好使了。结果就是我已经把要讲的细节忘得差不多了。所以接下来可能会显得有点生疏。

cues.en: But part of the purpose of this presentation is to present you with just the information that matters without a lot of the distracting details. And so I will actually rewrite all of my notes for this as we go. It's going to be a little bit rough, but hopefully it'll be an opportunity for us to focus just on what really matters and for us to put aside a lot of the associated implementation details and things which, frankly, it matters when you care about them, but it's not part of that core lesson of understanding Python.
cues.zh: 但我这次演讲的部分目的，就是只为大家呈现关键信息，剔除大量干扰细节。因此，我会在讲的过程中当场重写所有笔记。虽然会显得有点粗糙，但希望这能让我们专注于真正重要的核心内容，先抛开大量相关的实现细节，坦白讲，那些细节在你需要关注时确实重要，但并不是理解 Python 的核心课。

cues.en: I want to start off with something very simple. And you can see I created a directory called data model. And I'll just create a simple file in here. I want to create a class. And we're going to do all of this. Everything in this course will be, or everything in this session will be in Python 3.6. It'll be in Python 3.6 just for my own convenience, just so that I don't have to worry about all the details that might differ between Python 2 and Python 3. There's no particular reason why I choose Python 3 versus Python 2 for the purposes of what I'm going to show you.
cues.zh: 我想先从一个非常简单的例子讲起。大家可以看到我创建了一个名为 data model 的目录。我直接在里面建一个简单的文件。我想创建一个类。我们所有的操作都会在这里完成。本次课程或本次分享中的所有内容都将使用 Python 3.6。使用 Python 3.6 纯粹是为了我自己方便，省得去操心 Python 2 和 Python 3 之间的各种差异细节。单就我要演示的内容而言，选择 Python 3 而不是 Python 2 并没有什么特别的原因。

cues.en: Other than, it's the Python that I happen to use, and it's the Python that happens to be, there's some political reasons behind why Python two or three, but even skipping that is just for my own convenience, it's just to simplify things. So let's start with something very simple. I have some class. I want to do some kind of mathematical operation. I have some piece of software I write, and I have some class here that represents a polynomial. Some simple, you know, linear polynomial with various coefficients.
cues.zh: 除了这是我碰巧在用的 Python，而且它刚好就在这儿之外，在选 Python 2 还是 3 上其实有些站队的原因，不过撇开这些不谈，这纯粹是为了我方便、为了把事情讲得简单点。那我们就从一个非常简单的东西开始。我写了个类，想要做某种数学运算。我写了这么个软件，里面有个表示多项式的类。就是一个简单的、带不同系数的线性多项式。

cues.en: And I want to represent it as a Python object. And so I start with some code that looks like this, right? Class polynomial doesn't have anything interesting to it. And I can create two polynomials very simply. And I might say P1 has coefficients 1, 2, and 3, right? So this would be x squared plus 2x plus 3. And P2 has coefficients 3, 4, and 3. So this would be 3x squared, oops.
cues.zh: 我想把它表示成一个 Python 对象。所以我的初始代码大概长这样，对吧？Polynomial 类本身没有什么特别之处。我可以很轻松地创建两个多项式。比如 P1 的系数是 1、2 和 3，对吧？也就是 x 方加 2x 加 3。而 P2 的系数是 3、4 和 3。那它就是 3x 方，哎呀。

cues.en: plus 4x plus 3. Okay? And I want to be able to do some simple things that we did in math class with these. I want to be able to add them. I want to be able to subtract them. I want to be able to, you know, figure out some details of them. The very first thing for those of you who are relatively effective Python programmers is you're going to look at this and you're going to say, why on earth did you write that in four lines when you could have written it in two lines? Why did I write this in four lines here when I could have written it in two lines? How would I compact my code here? So instead of
cues.zh: 加 4x 加 3，对吧？我希望能用它们做一些我们在数学课上学过的简单操作。我希望能让它们相加，希望能让它们相减，希望能搞清楚它们的一些细节。对于在座比较熟练的 Python 程序员来说，看到这里的第一反应肯定是：你明明可以用两行写完，为什么非要写成四行？我这里为什么要写四行，明明两行就够了？我该怎么精简这里的代码呢？所以与其

cues.en: constructing my two polynomials and then initializing the coefficients, I could initialize them all together. What would I do? I'm trying to get you to give me a little bit of feedback here. So what would I do? What am I missing here? My class has nothing in its body. What is it missing to allow me to do this little bit more conveniently? A little bit louder for me. I need an init method. And so the very first thing when some of you look at this is you say, hold on, you're wasting our time here. You probably want to have an init method that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 先构造出两个多项式再初始化系数，我还不如一次性把它们全初始化好。那我该怎么做？我想听听大家的想法。那我该怎么做呢？这里漏了什么？我的类体里空空如也。它少了什么才能让我写起来更方便一点？大声一点告诉我。我需要一个 init 方法。所以你们有些人看到这里的第一反应就是：等等，你这是在浪费我们的时间，你八成是想要一个长成这样的 init 方法。

cues.en: So you can write these lines much more tersely. And you don't have to have four lines when two lines would do. All right? So now we're happy. Whoops. So now we're happy. Now, if I run my code, and I'll split my screen, shrink this a little bit, and I'll maybe print out, actually I'll do this. So I'll run my code, and I have P1 and P2. And then somebody else looks at this and says, oh my goodness, print it out to the screen. That looks so ugly. What am I missing here?
cues.zh: 所以你可以把这几行写得更简练。两行能搞定的事，没必要写四行。对吧？现在搞定了。哎呀。现在搞定了。现在，如果我运行代码，我分个屏，稍微缩小一点，我也许可以打印出……其实我可以这么做。我运行代码，有了 P1 和 P2。然后别人看到这个会说，天哪，打印到屏幕上这玩意儿太难看了吧。我这里漏了什么？

cues.en: I'm missing another method. What am I missing? I'm missing a method that corresponds to what happens when I call this function at the top level repr to figure out the representation of my python object. Yes or no? Yes. So what method do I implement up here? I have some method called repr. Right? So I have some method here that returns a string that gives me the information, gives me a printable representation of this class
cues.zh: 我漏了另一个方法。漏了什么呢？我漏了一个对应顶级函数 repr 的方法，用来获取我 Python 对象的表示形式。对不对？是的。那我该在这里实现什么方法呢？我得写个叫 __repr__ 的方法。对吧？所以我在这一写个返回字符串的方法，用来提供信息，在屏幕上给出这个类的

cues.en: to the screen. And so I'll make this very easy. And so I'll run my code again. And we'll see, oh, there we go. Those are our two polynomials. Pretty straightforward. And we could write, we could make this print out a little bit prettier. We could see the x squared and the x and the constant term if we wanted to. But you can see this is a lot easier than just seeing the name of the class and its memory location. And we can continue down this exercise. Because the next thing I want to be able to do is I want to be able to add these together. And when I add them together, nothing happens.
cues.zh: 可打印表示。那我就写得简单点。然后我重新运行代码。我们能看到，哦，搞定了。这就是我们的两个多项式。非常直观。我们也可以写……让这个打印输出更好看一点。如果我们想的话，可以看到 x 的平方、x 项以及常数项。但你能看出来，这比只看到类名和它的内存地址要直观得多。我们可以继续做这个练习。因为接下来我想做的是把它们加在一起。但当我把它们相加时，什么都没发生。

cues.en: Python gives me an error. Unsupported operand types for plus. Polynomial, polynomial. But that doesn't make any sense. I know I can add polynomials. I did it all the time when I was in high school. How do I tell Python how to add polynomials? I have another method called add. And in my add method, I might return a brand new polynomial where I just give it all of dot coifs. Oh, they're not coifs. Where I just zip together and add each of
cues.zh: Python 报错了：加号不支持的操作数类型，Polynomial，Polynomial。但这根本说不通，我知道多项式是可以相加的，我高中的时候经常这么算。那我要怎么告诉 Python 该如何做多项式相加呢？我还有另一个叫 add 的方法。在我的 add 方法里，我可以返回一个全新的 Polynomial，把所有的 dot coifs 传给它——噢，不是 coifs。我只需要把它们 zip 缝合在一起，然后把每一项

cues.en: the individual items. So when I run that in my script here, P1 plus P2, it gives me a polynomial with 4x squared plus 6x plus 6. Now, what's the pattern that we see evolving here? For those of you who, off the top of your head, you didn't remember which of the underscore functions there are. For those of you who haven't ever seen these underscore functions before, you've begun to see some pattern. And what is that pattern? I have some behavior that I want to implement, and I write
cues.zh: 单独相加。所以当我在脚本里运行 P1 plus P2 时，它返回给我一个 4x 平方加 6x 加 6 的多项式。现在，我们在这里能看出什么规律呢？对于那些一时想不起有哪些下划线函数的同学，或者以前从没见过这些下划线函数的同学，你们已经开始发现某种规律了。那是什么规律呢？我想实现某种行为，然后我写了

cues.en: some underscore function. Some function that begins with two underscores and ends with two underscores. And for those of you who are Python programmers already, you might be familiar with these underscore functions. You might call them dunder methods or double underscore methods.
